_about: Friday: a quote card (1 slide). Saturday: a tip (5-slide carousel), alternating young adults and couples in library order. Quotes are original Intimova lines, attributed '— INTIMOVA'. Never put a famous person's name on a quote: misattributed quotes are common and we can't check them. Tips come from an intimova.ng article or a source in sources.json; if a tip uses a research finding, the source goes on the slide. Tips marked audience 'young-adults' speak to people who want pleasure but hide it out of shame: warm, never preachy, 'it's normal, own it'.

items.text: You are allowed to want *more than surviving.*
Choosing yourself isn't selfish. *It's where love starts.*
Pleasure isn't a reward you have to earn. *It's part of looking after you.*
Rest first. *Then let yourself want things.*
You don't need anyone's permission *to feel good.*
Love starts at home. *Sometimes home is you.*
The right person will ask what you like. *Start by knowing.*
Being tired of surviving *isn't the same as being done with love.*
Your body isn't a project to fix. *It's home.*
Closeness is built in small moments, *not big gestures.*
Desire doesn't always knock. *Sometimes you open the door.*
Soft is not weak. *Soft is brave.*
A safe heart is worth waiting for. *So is yours.*
You deserve to be looked at *like you're the whole night.*
Say what you want out loud. *Even if only to yourself first.*

items.title: Your first toy, without the guilt
items.angle: Curious for months but never pressed 'buy'? Start small, quiet and body-safe. It's not a lifetime commitment: you're learning what you enjoy.
items.notes: Space at least 6 weeks from a-where-to-start (Thursday) and choosing-your-first-toy (Tuesday).

items.title: One question for tonight
items.angle: Swap guessing for asking: one gentle question ('What's something you'd like more of?'), when to ask it (not mid-moment), and how to listen without defending.

items.title: For him: the best move is a question
items.angle: What films show isn't how most women get there; it's anatomy, not a flaw in anyone. So skip the guessing: ask what she likes, then listen without taking it personally.
items.notes: No anatomical words on slides. Space 6 weeks from intercourse-is-enough, not-from-intercourse-alone and a-not-from-sex-alone.

items.title: Stay a while
items.angle: The minutes after matter: put the phone down, stay close, talk. Couples who did reported higher satisfaction.

items.title: New partner, nervous? That's normal
items.angle: Nerves and pressure are the usual reasons things end sooner than you'd like. Slow down, breathe, make it about both of you, not a performance.
items.notes: Space 6 weeks from a-finish-too-fast, lasting-longer and t-last-longer-together.

items.title: Start earlier than the bedroom
items.angle: A message at lunchtime, a hand on the back at dinner, no rush at night. Anticipation is part of it.
items.notes: Space at least 6 weeks from Tuesday's slow-the-start carousel.

items.title: Dry sometimes? No shame in it
items.angle: It changes with your cycle, stress, sleep and some medicines, and it doesn't mean you're not attracted. Give it time, keep a water-based lube nearby, and see a doctor if it hurts.
items.notes: Space 6 weeks from a-dry-not-attracted and dryness-what-helps.

items.title: Bringing a toy into the bedroom
items.angle: Lead with 'us', choose it together, start with something small and simple, laugh if it's awkward.
items.notes: Space at least 6 weeks from Tuesday's bringing-up-toys and from t-ask-dont-guess.

items.title: Private isn't the same as ashamed
items.angle: Plain, unbranded delivery handed over to a name; rinse, dry and store your toy somewhere clean and private. Keeping it private is self-respect, not a secret to feel bad about.
items.notes: Cleaning and storage wording from https://intimova.ng/learn/toys-body-safe/how-to-use-a-vibrator ('store it somewhere clean and private').

items.title: One night, no phones
items.angle: Pick one night a week with phones in another room. Some weeks you'll only talk, and that counts.
items.notes: A suggestion, not a research claim. Don't add statistics.

items.title: Not in the mood? Start anyway, gently
items.angle: For many people desire shows up after closeness begins, not before. No pressure: a slow start, and permission to stop.
items.notes: Consent stays central: 'permission to stop' must be on a slide. Space 6 weeks from desire-comes-first and a-desire-gone.

items.title: The most romantic thing might be sleep
items.angle: Tired bodies don't want much. An early night together, no expectations, and see what follows.
items.notes: If citing kalmbach-2015-sleep, don't repeat Monday's sleep-has-nothing-to-do within 6 weeks.

items.title: How to ask for what you want (without it sounding like a complaint)
items.angle: A relaxed moment, clothes on, not mid-moment. Make it 'we're curious', not 'you're lacking'. One line to borrow.
items.notes: Space 6 weeks from a-bring-it-up and bringing-up-toys. No prices from the article.

items.title: Say what you want, one sentence at a time
items.angle: Practise alone first. Start with what you enjoy ('I love it when…'), not what's wrong. Short and warm.

items.title: Learn what you like before anyone asks
items.angle: You can't tell someone what you enjoy if you've never found out. Exploring on your own is learning, and it's yours.
items.notes: Keep it suggestive. Space 6 weeks from t-ya-first-toy-no-guilt.

items.title: Look after your toy, and it looks after you
items.angle: Wipe it clean after every use, water-based lubricant only, charge it before it's flat, store it clean.
items.notes: Care steps only as stated on the product pages (npm run products).

items.title: Keep one thing new
items.angle: A new place in the house, a new time of day, a new question. Small changes beat big gestures.
items.notes: Suggestive only. Space 6 weeks from Tuesday's keeping-things-new.

items.title: When one of you wants it more
items.angle: Different levels of desire are normal. Talk about closeness, not frequency; find the middle; no keeping score.

items.title: Less rush, more together
items.angle: Slow down, pause and breathe, make it about both of you and not 'the finish'. See a doctor if it worries you.
items.notes: Space at least 6 weeks from Monday's lasting-is-fixed and Tuesday's lasting-longer.

items.title: If it hurts, stop
items.angle: Pain is a signal: stop, use more lube, slow down, and if it keeps happening, see a doctor or a sexual health clinic.
items.notes: Space at least 6 weeks from Monday's pain-is-normal.
